adversarial_test_results.prompt:
FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present disclosure relates generally to dispensing devices, and more particularly to a hand-held dispenser for viscous materials such as adhesives, sealants and greases.

BACKGROUND
Dispensing devices of this kind commonly include a barrel that holds the material and a plunger that advances through the barrel to express the material through a nozzle. In many such devices the plunger is driven by a ratchet mechanism that is advanced by a trigger, so that each squeeze of the trigger ejects a metered quantity of material. A difficulty with these devices is that the ratchet can slip when the material is cold and its viscosity is high, and the plunger may then retreat slightly between strokes, drawing air into the barrel. Another difficulty is that the trigger linkage wears at its pivot, so that the metered quantity changes over the life of the tool. Attempts to solve these problems have included spring-loaded pawls, friction washers and replaceable ratchet strips, but each adds parts and cost, and none has proved reliable in the field.
There is accordingly a need for a dispensing device that maintains a constant metered output, that does not draw air into the barrel when the material is stiff, and that can be manufactured with few parts.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
In one aspect, a dispensing device comprises a barrel having an open rear end and a nozzle at a front end, and a plunger slidably received in the barrel. A rod 40 extends rearwardly from the plunger and carries a rack 42 along one side. A housing 44 is mounted at the rear end of the barrel and rotatably supports a pinion 46 that meshes with the rack 42. A trigger 48 is pivoted to the housing 44 at a pivot pin 50 and carries a pawl 52 that engages the pinion 46 when the trigger 48 is squeezed, and a return spring 54 urges the trigger 48 away from the housing 44. A brake shoe 56 is carried on the housing 44 and bears against the rod 40 to resist rearward movement of the plunger, and a release lever 58 lifts the pawl 52 from the pinion 46 so that the rod 40 can be retracted for refilling.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION
Referring to FIG. 1, the housing 44 is formed in two halves that are joined along a parting line by screws 60. The pinion 46 is journalled in the housing 44 on a stub axle 62 and has eight teeth 64. The rack 42 has a pitch that matches the teeth 64, and the engagement between the pawl 52 and the pinion 46 is arranged so that a full stroke of the trigger 48 advances the rod 40 by one tooth. The brake shoe 56 is seated in a recess 66 in the housing 44 and is biased against the rod 40 by a spring 68, so that the rod 40 can move forward but not backward. When the material in the barrel is stiff, the brake shoe 56 holds the rod 40 while the trigger 48 returns, and the pawl 52 rides over the teeth 64 without drawing the rod 40 back.
To operate the device, the user fills the barrel, fits the nozzle, and squeezes the trigger 48 repeatedly. Each stroke advances the rod 40 by one tooth, and the material is expelled through the nozzle. When the barrel is empty, the release lever 58 is pressed, the pawl 52 disengages from the pinion 46, and the rod 40 is pushed back into the barrel so that the device can be refilled.
